newsitem.title: GERMANY: German exporters expect to boost growth this year.
newsitem.headline: German exporters expect to boost growth this year.

text.p: German exporters expect to be the country's main growth engine again this year, the Association of Wholesalers and Exporters (BGA) said on Tuesday.
The trade surplus should increase again in 1997 as trade volume is expected to grow five percent, BGA president Michael Fuchs told a news conference.
Exports should rise six percent to 831 billion marks ($487.6 billion) and imports expand four percent to 714 billion marks.
"German enterprises are moving away from traditional markets to new growth markets," Fuchs said.
In 1996, trade volume grew 4.1 percent to 1.471 billion marks as exports rose 4.6 percent and imports rose 3.4 percent, he said.
The strength of the dollar as well as an upturn in economic growth and revived demand in eastern Europe are the main reasons for the sunny outlook, he said.
But Fuchs said he found the German government's forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth this year too optimistic.
The volume of German trade with central and eastern Europe grew 11 percent last year, and surpassed trade with North America for the first time, he said.

Globalisation is a great opportunity for the German economy. But Fuchs said he found shocking the current low level of investment. Even New Zealand received three billion marks in foreign investment in 1996, five times as much as Germany, he said.
He blamed protectionism, an inflexible labour market, high non-wage labour costs and a high level of bureaucracy for Germany's current troubles.

Referring to demonstrations by coal miners who were blocking Bonn's main avenue to protest against the curtailment of subsidies, Fuchs said the mines should be shut down. Germany cannot afford them anymore.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.704 German Marks)
